title: Pricing Resolution
readerIntent: Configure and resolve contextual prices without embedding them in Product.
priorKnowledge: Understand product identity and trusted commerce context.
summary: Price lists and price groups organize prices; resolution filters eligible entries and applies deterministic priority and specificity for the trusted context.

sections.heading: Scopes
items: Tenant and enterprise.
Storefront Site and Store.
Country, region, channel, currency, and locale.
Customer segment, price group, customer, contract, and promotion context.
Product/variant, unit, quantity tier, date range, and active state.

sections.heading: Price structures and responsibility
items: A PriceList is a governed collection with validity, currency, priority, and business scope. A PriceGroup lets several customers, segments, stores, or sites share eligibility without copying every price.
A Price is the sellable amount for a product or variant under declared conditions. Product owns identity and merchandising; Pricing owns monetary eligibility and resolution.
Currency, selling unit, quantity tier, tax treatment, discount metadata, and effective dates must remain explicit. A numeric amount without these qualifiers is not a complete enterprise price.
Storefront supplies trusted website context and Store supplies commercial relationships, but neither calculates or persists the resolved price.

sections.heading: Resolution
items: Normalize and validate trusted context.
Select active eligible price lists and price groups.
Filter prices by product, scope, currency, unit, quantity, and effective time.
Rank explicit priority and specificity deterministically.
Return price, tax/discount metadata, provenance, and safe explanation according to contract.
Reject ambiguous ties or apply a documented configurable rule.

sections.heading: Publishing and cache
items: Staged prices enter approval and nPublish deployment before Online use.
Cache keys include every context dimension that can change the result.
Price/group/list changes invalidate bounded affected projections; cache never becomes price authority.

sections.heading: Example, failures, and acceptance
items: Assume an iPhone has a general UAE web price, a Dubai Store price, and a negotiated enterprise-customer price. The resolver first removes entries with the wrong tenant, enterprise, currency, unit, date, channel, or customer eligibility.

Among eligible entries it applies configured priority and specificity. The negotiated customer entry wins only when the authenticated principal and trusted context prove that relationship; a browser-supplied customer code is insufficient.

If two entries are equally eligible and no documented tie-breaker exists, fail as ambiguous instead of silently choosing an unstable result. If no entry is eligible, return a deliberate not-priced outcome rather than zero.

Acceptance tests cover boundary dates, quantity tiers, unit compatibility, currency, store/site/segment specificity, unauthorized context injection, deterministic ties, staged-to-online publishing, invalidation, provider failure, and regression of existing prices.

sections.heading: Axis and BackOffice exposure
items: Pricing contributes its Commerce Operations navigation metadata from the backend. Axis renders Price Lists, Prices, Price Groups, and Price Assignments through reusable schema workbench components.
Promotions and Coupons remain planned until an owning backend capability exists; documentation and navigation must not imply those features are available.
Business-specific pricing dashboards should reuse the same query, grid, export, and detail components while keeping price resolution and mutation in Pricing services.

sections.heading: Permissions and security
items: BackOffice visibility is gated by `pricing.backoffice.read`; manage operations require explicit Pricing permissions and must be enforced by backend routes.
The resolver must ignore untrusted browser-supplied tenant, customer, segment, Store, Site, currency, and channel claims unless the backend proves them from authenticated context.
Price data, eligibility, and publication state are commercial controls. Audit manual overrides, imports, publishing actions, ambiguous resolution failures, and cache invalidation.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
items: Customer modules may add price dimensions, tie-break rules, validation, import/export data, projection logic, and BackOffice presentation metadata through later layers.
Do not copy prices into Product, Storefront, CMS, or Axis components. Those layers reference Pricing outcomes and remain consumers.

Verify custom Pricing behavior with resolver contract tests, boundary-date and unit tests, authorization tests, import/export checks, publication/cache invalidation checks, and rollback of the customer layer.
